svg.title: Quartiles from two equal halves of ten ordered observations
svg.desc: The ordered numerical observations are four, six, seven, nine, ten, twelve, fourteen, sixteen, eighteen and thirty. Use the explicitly stated median-of-halves convention. Because the count is even, all ten records remain: the first five form the lower half and the last five form the upper half. Their middle values give lower quartile seven and upper quartile sixteen. The overall median averages the values in positions five and six, ten and twelve, giving eleven. The interquartile range is sixteen minus seven, nine. A true-scale number line shows range thirty minus four, twenty-six, and interquartile range nine. Quartiles and extremes are distinct positions.
